title: Uniformly convergent continuous multipliers against an L¹ density vanishing off a compact set
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, ν a measure on ℝ^P, F : ℝ^P → ℝ ν-integrable, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with F(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous and g_k : ℝ^P → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) continuous with g_k → f uniformly on ℝ^P. Then ∫ g_k(x)F(x) dν(x) → ∫ f(x)F(x) dν(x) as k → ∞ (Bochner integrals).
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Eucl P)) (F : Eucl P → ℝ) (K : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (g : ℕ → Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable F ν → IsCompact K → (∀ x, x ∉ K → F x = 0) → Continuous f → (∀ k, Continuous (g k)) → TendstoUniformly g f atTop → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, g k x * F x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x * F x ∂ν))
